about.title: Built for people who show up
body: Titan Fitness opened in 2019 with a simple bet: if you give people real coaching and equipment that doesn't fall apart, they'll keep coming back. Six years later, that bet paid off.
We're not a franchise following a script. Every coach here is certified, every program is built around your goals, and every member gets checked in on — not just checked in.

blogPosts.title: How to Lose Weight Without Losing Your Mind
blogPosts.excerpt: The unglamorous, highly effective basics that actually move the needle — and why most fad plans fail.
blogPosts.author: Coach Priya
content: Most people don't fail at weight loss because they lack willpower — they fail because the plan they picked was never sustainable past week three.
Start with the boring fundamentals: a modest, consistent calorie deficit, protein at every meal, and 2–3 strength sessions a week to protect muscle mass while you lose fat.
Track weekly averages, not daily fluctuations — water weight and sodium will lie to you day-to-day, but a 7-day average rarely does.
Finally, pick a program you can still be doing in six months. The "best" diet is the one you actually stick to.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: We collect the information you provide when you sign up for a membership or contact us — name, email, phone number, and billing details necessary to process payments.

sections.heading: How we use it
sections.body: Your information is used to manage your membership, communicate about classes and schedule changes, and process payments. We do not sell member data to third parties.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can request a copy of the data we hold about you, or ask us to delete it, at any time by emailing us or asking at the front desk.

sections.heading: Membership terms
sections.body: Memberships are billed monthly and can be cancelled with 30 days notice. Freezes of up to 30 days per year are available at no extra charge.

sections.heading: Facility use
sections.body: Members are expected to re-rack weights, wipe down equipment after use, and follow posted class capacity limits.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: Exercise carries inherent risk. Members are responsible for training within their own physical limits and consulting a physician before starting a new program if needed.
